The audit release candidate. A full audit of `develop` (panel, agent and
installer) raised 163 findings; each is closed by a commit with a test checked
against the code, a few more by a run on a live stand, two are carried as
named risks until the refactor after this release, and one minor finding is
moved past it. Three features land that the subscription side was missing:
operator subscription templates, the operator's own routing presets, and a
host that can carry a description or be hidden. One profile can now sit on a
node on several ports. Over 300 commits since v0.2.1.

This is a release candidate: run it on a stand or a node you can rebuild before
a production fleet.

## Upgrading

Update the panel and every node agent together. The new agent reports its
cores per adapter and the old panel cannot read that; the new panel pushes
users in batches the old agent does not have (it falls back to one request per
user, slowly, but works). An agent from before this release cannot rotate its
mTLS certificate: the node page says so and asks for the update.

The agent still has no self-update. After deploying the panel, rebuild the
agent on every node over SSH (`git fetch`, `go build`, restart), as for v0.2.1.

Expect these once, right after the update:

- The first restart of the new agent reconnects AmneziaWG clients one time: the
  old agent kept no state file to carry the peers over. Later restarts keep
  them.
- The first push to an updated node restarts Xray one time (it gains the
  routing service that later swaps rules live) and rewrites the sing-box
  config.
- On a node where an old agent left `mita` running with no mieru profile, the
  first push stops it.
- The first stats poll does not count about one poll interval of traffic per
  user and node: the snapshots move to a key per adapter.
- A VLESS cascade leg stored without REALITY gets it on the next push of its
  cascade, on both ends at once, without anyone resaving the cascade.
- Users of Clash-family, sing-box, Loon and Quantumult X apps see new lines
  after their next refresh where a cascade entry is in their subscription (see
  Cascades below).

On a node installed before this release, the agent sets Hysteria's log level
with a runtime drop-in, so Hysteria restarts once shortly after every reboot
of that node. Nodes installed or reinstalled with this release carry the level
in the unit and are not restarted; a node where only the agent was rebuilt
stays on the drop-in.

The migration that lets one profile take several ports on a node
(`20261025164819_binding_many_ports`) rolls back only while no profile holds a
second port on any node.

## Privacy

The audit found that nodes and the panel kept more about users than they
should. All of it is closed in this release; what earlier versions left behind
stays on your servers until you remove it.

- **Nodes no longer journal connections.** Earlier agents let Xray write a
  line per connection to the node's journal (the client's IP, the destination
  and the user), and Hysteria a line per connect and disconnect (the client's
  IP and the user). The new agent turns the Xray access log off and runs
  Hysteria at `warn`, on nodes installed before as well; NaiveProxy leaves the
  proxy's error lines, which named the client and the destination, out of its
  log. MTProto (mtg)
  still names the client's IP when a connection fails; it has no quieter level.
- **Clearing what older agents left.** The node page tells whether the node's
  journal still holds such lines, and since when, and can clear it. journald
  and syslog cannot be cleared selectively: this removes the node's whole
  journal and syslog, so the choice is yours, node by node. By hand:
  `journalctl --rotate && journalctl --vacuum-time=1s` and
  `truncate -c -s 0 /var/log/syslog && rm -f /var/log/syslog.*`.
- **The panel's logs no longer hold subscription tokens.** Earlier versions
  logged every subscription poll with the full token and the subscriber's IP,
  and the node bootstrap token, in the backend log, the frontend's nginx log
  and the host Caddy's access log. The backend now masks any `:token` path
  segment and cuts the requester's address to /24 or /48; nginx and Caddy
  write those requests to a masked log. Container logs are capped at 10 MB x 3.
  Updating recreates the panel's containers, which removes their old logs
  (unless Docker on the host sends container logs elsewhere, such as journald);
  the host Caddy's old `/var/log/caddy/access.log` is yours to clear. Tokens are
  not reissued for you: if those logs may have left your hands, reissue the
  subscription links of the users concerned.
- **Deleting a user deletes it.** A user deleted in the panel is erased for
  good 30 days later, with their traffic history, devices, keys and
  subscription polls. The first daily cleanup after the update (03:30, panel
  server time) erases at once every user deleted more than 30 days before it.
- **Devices are forgotten.** A device not seen for 90 days is removed and no
  longer counts towards the user's device limit.
- **The subscription page does not send its address as a referrer,** and its
  links out carry `noreferrer`, so the subscription address does not travel to
  the next site.

## Cascades

- **Every format that carries VLESS now hands out the cascade routes.**
  Clash, mihomo and Stash, sing-box, Loon and Quantumult X clients receive one
  line per exit, named by the exit, with the route tag in the UUID, as the
  share links and the xray-json array already did. Before, these formats
  handed out the cascade entry itself, and traffic left from the entry's
  country. Surge carries no VLESS and gets no routes.
- **Only VLESS selects an exit.** A trojan or vmess host on a cascade entry
  cannot carry the route in its credential: its users connect and leave from
  the entry's country, and the cascade screen names such profiles. Trojan share
  links, and trojan and vmess in the xray-json array, used to come as one line
  per exit with an altered credential, which the entry refused; they now come
  as one plain line.
  Use VLESS on the entry for exit selection.
- **A node stands in one enabled cascade.** A second enabled cascade on a node
  that already has one is refused with `409 NODE_IN_OTHER_CASCADE`, naming the
  node and the cascade. Overlaps saved before stay saved, but the oldest
  cascade keeps the node and every younger one that shares a node is treated
  as switched off as a whole: it is drawn on none of its nodes and its lines
  leave its users' subscriptions. The panel log at start and a Telegram notice
  name them.
- **A transit with two or more directions on a leg that is not VLESS carries no
  traffic.** It used to send every direction out of the first one. The panel
  log at start and a Telegram notice name such cascades: move that hop to VLESS
  or keep one direction.
- **Cascade exits for a user in several squads are granted by the squads that
  hand that entry out.** An open squad beside a narrow one gives every exit;
  the narrow one no longer takes exits away. Such users may see more
  subscription lines.

## Nodes and hosts

- **One profile on several ports of a node.** A host can put its profile on a
  port the node does not serve it on yet, and that becomes a binding of its
  own. Changing a host's port now moves that host alone by default; moving the
  whole binding with its other hosts is a choice made before the save.
- **Several inbounds of one core on a node** work for Xray, mieru, and the
  sing-box tuic, AnyTLS, Hysteria 2, Shadowsocks, ShadowTLS and Xray-protocol
  adapters. A second inbound of a single-inbound adapter (native Shadowsocks on
  Xray, Hysteria, AmneziaWG of one generation, NaiveProxy, MTProto) is refused
  in words before the save. The node's sync status names slot conflicts and
  where a squad's limit on a user does not hold on that core.
- **The agent closes the ufw port of an inbound the cores no longer hold.** A
  plain operator allow rule for the same port and protocol goes with it; rules
  with a source or destination stay, and port 22 and the agent's own port are
  never touched. An Xray inbound on kcp is opened over UDP.
- **The node's mTLS certificate can be renewed** from the node page, and the
  panel renews it before it expires.
- **The node and panel installers no longer fail on Ubuntu with automatic
  updates running** (already on `main`, which the installers pull).

## Node policies

`POST`/`PUT /api/node-policies` answers 400 with the field path for an address
among the domains or the other way round, `ip:` and `cidr:` prefixes, a port
range with an en dash or port 0, and a protocol outside http, tls, quic,
bittorrent. A rule saved before goes to the node with its readable conditions
only, and not at all when a whole kind of condition is lost (it used to become
a rule on all traffic). Saving a policy that still holds such a rule is refused
until the rule is fixed.

## Users and subscriptions

- **Delivery numbers change.** The host card for who still holds an old link
  counts a change by the link's own stamp (filled from the last update on
  existing rows) and counts only active users. A poll is now only a request
  from a client app: the user's view in the panel and the subscription page in
  a browser no longer count, which the user's delivery card reads.
- **MTProto users no longer show online,** and have no last node or first
  connection: the shared secret does not tell users apart.
- `?node=` in wgconf, AmneziaVPN and Outline links is now the endpoint id; old
  links by label are still accepted.

## API

- **Refusals name what they hit.** Creating a user that loses a race says
  `USERNAME_TAKEN`, `SUBSCRIPTION_TOKEN_TAKEN` or `SOURCE_ID_TAKEN` with
  `field`, `SHORT_ID_TAKEN`, or `UNIQUE_CONFLICT` with the index named in the
  message; a taken username used to be a plain `CONFLICT`. Region and route
  policy conflicts carry `field`. A name race on a squad, profile, geo set or
  named outbound is a 409, not a 500, and so is a write a foreign key refuses
  (`REFERENCED`).
- `PUT /api/hosts/:id` with a new `port` moves only that host
  (`portMove: "host"`); `portMove: "binding"` moves the binding with its hosts.
  `409 HOST_PORT_SHARED` is gone, and `confirmSharedPort` is read as
  `portMove: "binding"`.
- The template dry run returns its warnings as `{ code, message }` objects, and
  the import answer no longer carries `rewrittenKeys`.
- **Per-user traffic on every sing-box protocol** needs the panel's own sing-box
  1.13.14 build (`core-singbox-v1.13.14`), which the installer sets up.

## Subscription templates

Templates for mihomo, Stash, legacy Clash, sing-box and Xray JSON live under
Subscription, Templates. With no template in force the output is byte for byte
what it was. The Clash family now answers by core: `mihomo`, `stash` and
`clash-legacy` are formats of their own, and `clash` stays mihomo byte for byte.
A host switched off for `clash` before the update is switched off for all four;
after it, switching `clash` off on a host switches `clash` and `mihomo` off
together, and Stash is set on its own.

- `?template=<name>` picks a template; a format without templates answers 400,
  an unknown name 404.
- `/sub/<token>/<client>` names the format in the path (`mihomo`, `stash`,
  `clash`, `singbox`, `json`, `base64`, `raw`), ahead of the User-Agent rules.
- `?format=raw` gives the share links without base64.
- A User-Agent rule can name the template its clients get.
- The dry run checks a template with the real core only where the panel has a
  sing-box or Xray binary. The panel image carries none, so an installed panel
  answers "not checked by the core"; the warnings about nodes left out of every
  group work everywhere. There is no Clash-family core on the panel at all.
- Templates from another panel import as a draft. Run them through
  `iceslab-migrate templates` first: it renames the service key to Iceslab's.
  sing-box templates written with the old DNS format import, but sing-box 1.13
  and later refuses them unless `ENABLE_DEPRECATED_LEGACY_DNS_SERVERS` is set,
  and the dry run of an installed panel does not catch it: move the DNS block
  to the new format before use.

A host can carry a one-line description (shown by the apps that support it)
and can be hidden from every public output unless a template asks for hidden
hosts.
